questions.question: Which of these is most like a torch BEAM?
questions.explanation: A ray has one endpoint (the torch) and extends without end.

questions.question: Which of these is most like a stretched rubber band fixed at both ends?
questions.explanation: Two endpoints + a definite length = line segment.

questions.question: Which is NOT a valid name for the angle whose vertex is Q with arms going through P and R?
questions.explanation: In ∠PRQ, the middle letter is R, but the vertex is Q. The vertex must be in the middle.

questions.question: Three quarters of a turn equals how many degrees?
Half a turn plus a quarter turn is:
Classify an angle of 60°.
Classify an angle of 175°.
questions.explanation: 175° is between 90° and 180° → obtuse (just below straight).

questions.question: Classify an angle of 0°.
questions.explanation: An angle of 0° is the zero angle — both arms point the same way.

questions.question: Which list is in order from smallest to largest type of angle?
questions.explanation: <90°, =90°, between 90° and 180°, between 180° and 360°.

questions.question: The symbol AB ∥ CD is read:
questions.explanation: The double-bar symbol ∥ means parallel.

questions.question: The symbol AB ⊥ CD is read:
options: AB intersects CD at any angle
questions.explanation: The ⊥ symbol denotes perpendicular (90°) intersection.

questions.question: Two intersecting lines that are NOT perpendicular form how many right angles among their four angles?
questions.explanation: If even one of the four angles were 90°, the others (vertically opposite + linear pair) would all be 90° → perpendicular. Since they are NOT perpendicular, no angle is 90°.

questions.question: Two lines intersect. One angle is 25°. The angle next to it (linear pair) is:
Two lines cross. The four angles are 50°, 130°, 50°, ____. Find the missing angle.
questions.explanation: Vertically opposite to the 130° angle is also 130°.

questions.question: Two lines intersect. The sum of two ADJACENT angles (forming a linear pair) is:
questions.explanation: By definition of linear pair.

questions.question: If two lines intersect and one angle is 60°, what is the SUM of all four angles?
questions.explanation: All four angles around a point sum to 360°. Here: 60° + 120° + 60° + 120° = 360°.

questions.question: Which everyday object's corner is closest to a STRAIGHT angle?
options: the tip of a pencil sharpened to a point
a fully open laptop lid lying flat with its base
the corner of a slice of pizza
questions.answer: a fully open laptop lid lying flat with its base
questions.explanation: When a laptop's lid is fully open and flat with the base, it forms a 180° (straight) angle.

questions.question: Which of these is closest to a RIGHT angle?
questions.explanation: At 3:00 the hour and minute hands are exactly 90° apart (right angle).

questions.question: A line segment is part of a line.
questions.explanation: A line segment is the piece of a line between two endpoints.

questions.question: The size of an angle changes if you make its arms longer.
questions.explanation: Angle size depends on the OPENING between the arms, not the arm length.

questions.question: Every right angle is also an acute angle.
questions.explanation: Acute means strictly less than 90°. A right angle is exactly 90°, not acute.

questions.question: Perpendicular lines are a special case of intersecting lines.
questions.explanation: All perpendicular lines intersect — at exactly 90°.

questions.question: Parallel lines can also be perpendicular.
questions.explanation: Parallel lines never meet; perpendicular lines meet at 90°. They are mutually exclusive.

questions.question: When two lines cross, the four angles always add up to 360°.
questions.explanation: All angles around a single point sum to 360°.

questions.question: A line segment has ____ endpoints.
questions.explanation: Endpoints at each end.

questions.question: We measure angles using a tool called a ____.
questions.explanation: A half-circle measuring tool.

questions.question: An angle of exactly 180° is called a ____ angle.
questions.explanation: Half a turn.

questions.question: Lines that never meet are called ____ lines.
questions.explanation: By definition.

questions.question: If one angle of a linear pair is 50°, the other is ____°.
Two lines intersect. If one angle is 100°, the angle directly OPPOSITE is ____°.
questions.explanation: Vertically opposite angles are equal.

questions.question: Look at this figure (described): two rays meet at point M. One arm passes through K, the other through L. Write all valid names of this angle.
questions.answer: Three valid names: ∠KML, ∠LMK, and ∠M (since only one angle has vertex M). The order of K and L doesn't matter, but M MUST be in the middle when using three letters.
questions.explanation: Vertex must be the middle letter; arms can be in either order.

questions.question: Describe step-by-step how to draw an angle of 75° using a protractor.
questions.answer: (1) Draw a horizontal ray with endpoint V (the vertex). (2) Place the centre of the protractor on V; align its 0° line with the ray. (3) Find the 75° mark on the appropriate scale (inner or outer, whichever starts at 0° on your aligned arm) and make a small dot. (4) Lift the protractor; draw a ray from V through the dot. The two rays form a 75° angle.
questions.explanation: Same procedure as for any specific-measure angle.

questions.question: Classify each angle and give a real-world example: (i) 30°, (ii) 90°, (iii) 150°.
questions.answer: (i) 30°: acute. Example: a small slice of pizza. (ii) 90°: right angle. Example: the corner of a book or door frame. (iii) 150°: obtuse. Example: the angle between the arms of an open clothes-peg.
questions.explanation: Connecting maths to everyday objects.

questions.question: Give one real-world example each for: (i) parallel lines, (ii) intersecting lines, (iii) perpendicular lines.
questions.answer: (i) Parallel: railway tracks; opposite edges of a ruler. (ii) Intersecting (any angle): the letter 'X'; two roads crossing. (iii) Perpendicular: corners of a notebook; the cross arms of a + symbol.
questions.explanation: Many correct answers; the categories are clear.

questions.question: Two lines intersect; one of the angles is 110°. Find the other three angles. Use the rules and explain.
questions.answer: Vertically opposite to 110° is 110° (vertically opposite angles are equal). The two angles adjacent to 110° (linear pairs) are 180° − 110° = 70° each. Other three angles: 70°, 110°, 70°.
questions.explanation: Apply the two key rules — vertically opposite equal, linear pair sums to 180°.

questions.question: Two intersecting lines form four angles. One of them is acute. Without computing, decide: are the OTHER three angles also acute?
questions.answer: No. If one angle is acute (less than 90°), then the angle next to it (linear pair) is 180° minus an acute angle, which is GREATER than 90° — so it is obtuse. So we get TWO acute angles (the original and its vertically-opposite partner) and TWO obtuse angles (the two linear-pair partners).
questions.explanation: Linear pair turns acute into obtuse.

questions.question: Sketch (in words) all five named types of angle: acute, right, obtuse, straight, reflex.
questions.answer: Acute (e.g. 45°): two arms forming a small narrow V. Right (90°): two arms perpendicular like the corner of a book. Obtuse (e.g. 130°): two arms forming a wide V, more open than a corner. Straight (180°): two arms in opposite directions, forming a single straight line. Reflex (e.g. 280°): the LARGE angle on the outside, more than half a turn.
questions.explanation: Visual descriptions for each named type.

questions.question: Two lines intersect. The four angles are labelled in order around the intersection: ∠1, ∠2, ∠3, ∠4. Given ∠1 = 65°, find ∠2, ∠3 and ∠4. State which rule (vertically opposite or linear pair) you used for each.
questions.answer: ∠2 is adjacent to ∠1 → linear pair: ∠2 = 180° − 65° = 115°. ∠3 is opposite ∠1 → vertically opposite: ∠3 = 65°. ∠4 is adjacent to ∠1 (other side) → linear pair: ∠4 = 180° − 65° = 115°. (Equivalently ∠4 is vertically opposite to ∠2.) So ∠1 = 65°, ∠2 = 115°, ∠3 = 65°, ∠4 = 115°.
questions.explanation: Practises naming the rule used at each step.

questions.question: Suppose you need to draw a 210° angle using a standard 0–180° protractor. Describe a method to do it (the protractor only goes up to 180°!).
questions.answer: Trick: 210° = 360° − 150°, OR 210° = 180° + 30°. So draw a STRAIGHT line through the vertex (this represents the 180° part). Then, on the same side as you want the 'extra 30°', draw a 30° angle to one of the arms, measured with the protractor in the usual way. The COMBINED opening on that side is 180° + 30° = 210°. Equivalently, the OTHER side (the 'small' angle) is 360° − 210° = 150°; a straight line plus a 30° angle on one side.
questions.explanation: 210° is reflex, so it's the 'big' angle. We split it as 180° + 30° because the protractor maxes at 180°.

questions.question: A student claims: 'Two lines intersect, and one of the four angles is 200°.' Is this possible? Justify carefully.
questions.answer: If we measure the ANGLE between the two arms at the intersection (the smaller of the two openings), it is between 0° and 180°. So a single 'interior' angle of 200° is NOT possible at a simple intersection in the usual sense. However, you CAN describe the REFLEX angle on the OUTSIDE of the intersection as 200° — but the 'four angles' at a normal intersection are typically the four interior angles, all between 0° and 180°. So in the standard sense the student is wrong; if they meant the reflex angle, it could be 200° but then the four interior angles still sum to 360° and the corresponding interior angle would be 360° − 200° = 160°.
questions.explanation: Tests careful reading: distinguishes 'interior' angles at intersection from reflex measures.

questions.question: Which of these geometric objects has both finite length AND a specific direction?
questions.explanation: A segment has two endpoints (finite length); a ray has direction but no finite length.

questions.question: Through how many degrees does the minute hand of a clock move in 30 minutes?
questions.explanation: 30 minutes = half a turn = 180°.

questions.question: The minute hand of a clock moves through how many degrees in 15 minutes?
questions.explanation: 15 min = quarter turn = 90°.

questions.question: Two angles are SUPPLEMENTARY if they add up to 180°. If one is 67°, the other is:
Two angles are COMPLEMENTARY if they add up to 90°. If one is 35°, the other is:
Which statement is ALWAYS true?
options: Two perpendicular lines are also parallel.
Two intersecting lines are always perpendicular.
Two lines must always be parallel.
questions.explanation: Definition of parallel.

questions.question: Vertically opposite angles are:
questions.explanation: By the vertically-opposite angles rule.

questions.question: An angle of 89° is a right angle.
questions.explanation: A right angle is exactly 90°. 89° is acute (just below right).

questions.question: If two lines do not intersect, they are necessarily parallel (in flat geometry).
questions.explanation: In a single plane, two non-intersecting lines must be parallel.

questions.question: A reflex angle measures more than 180° but less than ____°.
questions.explanation: Reflex range: (180°, 360°).

questions.question: Two lines intersect to form four angles. Two adjacent angles are (4y)° and (5y + 27)°. Find y, and then state all four angles.
questions.answer: (4y) + (5y + 27) = 180 → 9y + 27 = 180 → 9y = 153 → y = 17. Angles: 4y = 68°; 5y + 27 = 112°. The other pair (vertically opposite) repeats: 68° and 112°. Four angles: 68°, 112°, 68°, 112°.
questions.explanation: Linear pair sums to 180°; solve the resulting equation.

questions.question: Find the supplementary angle of 47° and the complementary angle of 47°.
questions.explanation: Supplementary pairs sum to 180°; complementary pairs sum to 90°.

questions.question: Look at a clock. Estimate the angle between the hour and minute hands at (i) 6:00, (ii) 9:00, (iii) 12:00.
questions.answer: (i) 6:00 — hour hand at 6, minute hand at 12 → angle = 180° (straight). (ii) 9:00 — hour hand at 9, minute hand at 12 → angle = 90° (right). (iii) 12:00 — both hands together → angle = 0° (zero).
questions.explanation: Each hour mark on a clock is 30° apart (360°/12).

questions.question: How would you draw an angle of 0° using a protractor? What does it look like?
questions.answer: An angle of 0° has the two arms pointing in the SAME direction — they overlap. To draw, just draw a single ray; mark the vertex; the 'two arms' coincide. The protractor isn't really needed for this special case.
questions.explanation: Zero angle is degenerate — the two arms have not 'opened up' from each other yet.

questions.question: Identify three angles you can SEE in your classroom or home, and classify each as acute, right, obtuse, straight, or reflex.
questions.answer: Examples: (1) The corner of a desk → right (90°). (2) An open book lying flat with the pages spread → close to straight (180°) or obtuse if not fully open. (3) The hands of a clock at 2:00 → about 60° (acute). Many correct answers; rubric checks the classification matches the description.
questions.explanation: Encourages observation of angles in the everyday world.
